entities.summary: Gender history is a sub-field of history and gender studies, which looks at the past from the perspective of gender. It is in many ways, an outgrowth of women's history. The discipline considers in what ways historical events and periodization impact women differently from men. For instance, in an influential article in 1977, "Did Women have a Renaissance?", Joan Kelly questioned whether the notion of a Renaissance was relevant to women. Gender historians are also interested in how gender difference has been perceived and configured at different times and places, usually with the assumption that such differences are socially constructed.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gender history has significantly impacted our understanding of women's roles in historical societies, challenging traditional narratives and shedding light on the experiences of women across cultures. By examining gender differences as socially constructed, historians can better contextualize women's lives and contributions.
